institutionName: University of Natural Resources and Life Sciences, Vienna (BOKU)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The courses offered at the host university. A city I wanted to live in.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy to find information needed upon arrival from email from both UCPH and the host university as well as on UCPH and the host university websites.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were some orientation days for the incoming students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was bit difficult because there are many students looking at the same. It is necessary to start early and have enough time to check daily the rooms that are available.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: BOKU is in the 18th and 19th districts. You don't need to live in one of those districts but when looking for an accomodation you should check how public transports can take you to the campuses.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: As I am a double degree student I had to do the full students registration at BOKU.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Information in email, on the website and possibility to ask questions by email or in person if you go to the office.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Registering for classes was quite easy, there was a few bugs but I just emailed the professors of the classes I wanted to take and it worked.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just follow the guidelines

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took only MA level courses. The level were more or less the same as at UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There are several type of classes at BOKU : Lecture, Seminar (discussion and presentation type of class), Exercices, Mix of Lecture and Exercices.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Plant and environment 
Ecology of aquatic systems
Master's thesis seminar 
Mountain forest climatology and headwater hydrology
Soil ecology
Seminar in global change and ecosystems
Formulation of questions and experimental design in ecological research
Decision support systems
Microbial ecology and geomicrobiology
Frontiers in social ecology and sustainability transformations

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer: Master thesis

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Formulation of questions and experimental design in ecological research is a really good methodoly class.
Frontiers in social ecology and sustainability transformations is an easy, really interesting class for social aspects of sustainability.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I didn't encounter any unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Globally, everything is less expensive that in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I took sports courses and they were good.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many sports, movie projections, participating in a communal garden.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Depend on the tastes.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Try some hikes around Vienna, visit the city center and a few museums.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was really easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Try to join a non-academic activity you like, sign up for exercices or seminar classes because there is usually less students than in lecture so it's easier to socialize.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The closing of everything on Sundays, some places only accept cash.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The architecture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Start looking for accomodation early, learn to have cash on yourself to pay and enjoy.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't think so.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: My master thesis.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Learning a bit of german.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
